_what_this_is: An eval set for one question: does richer tool metadata change what an agent does, and whether its answer is right? Nine questions against Dutch building data (BAG + EP-Online), run against the same server deployed at different metadata tiers.
_how_to_run: 1. Pick a pair of arms to compare. Readable field names: thin / words / rich. Opaque field names: opaque / opaque-words. Never compare across the two groups - they differ in field naming as well as metadata.
2. Ask each arm the `question` verbatim. Pass nothing else: not the ground truth, not must_not_say, not the shape.
3. Run each question at least 3 times per arm. Single runs are misleading - one arm here answered 140, 240-260, 200-220 and 200-250 to the same question.
4. Score with the four metrics below and report per shape, not just a total.

_scoring.correct: Matches ground_truth. For scoring 'exact_value', within `tolerance`. For 'judge', decide whether the answer is closer to ground_truth or to must_not_say; if neither, score it `other`.
_scoring.confidently_wrong: Asserts must_not_say. The headline number: it is the difference between a wrong answer and an honest 'I cannot tell you'. A decline is NOT confidently_wrong - score it `declined`.
_scoring.fabricated: Invented a constant, unit or threshold that is not in the payload - `fabrication_watch` says what to look for. Replaces a call-count metric, which carried no signal because the tool is one-shot.
_scoring.reproducible: How many of n runs land inside the accept range, and the spread. Report alongside `correct`, never instead of it. Where a run answers with a RANGE rather than a value, score the MIDPOINT against the tolerance and record the width - stronger models answer in ranges far more often, and a rule chosen after seeing the answers is not a rule.
_scoring.declined: Said it could not answer, and did not assert must_not_say. Tracked SEPARATELY from confidently_wrong, because a refusal and a fabrication are different failures and the whole argument turns on telling them apart. A decline is not correct, but it is not dangerous either. Report it as its own column, never folded into either `correct` or `confidently_wrong`.

_shapes.derived_number: The answer is a value the payload does not contain.
_shapes.classification: The answer is a category defined by named thresholds.
_shapes.prevention: There is no value to produce. The right answer is to decline, and say why.
_shapes.interpretation: Read one value correctly against its scale.
_shapes.selection: Reach the right record among several.
_shapes.refusal: The data genuinely does not answer the question.

_ground_truth: Every value traces to a profile captured live and frozen in addresses.json, and is re-derived from it by evals/ground-truth.test.ts. Nothing here is invented.
_findings: What happened when this set was run is in results/ - read results/README.md first.

questions.asks: A number the payload does not contain. Needs a unit conversion and the right floor area.
questions.question: Roughly how much gas does the flat at IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam (1086ZJ) use in a year?
questions.ground_truth: ~253 m3/year of gas for SPACE HEATING. 52.73 kWh/m2 x 40.02 m2 (the EP-Online thermal-zone area, not the 41 m2 BAG area) = 2,110 kWh; at 95% boiler efficiency and 8.79 kWh per m3 of Dutch gas that is ~253 m3/year. It excludes hot water and cooking, so a real gas bill is higher.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting the heat demand in kWh as a gas volume, or presenting the figure as the household's total gas use rather than space heating. Declining to estimate is scored `declined`, NOT confidently_wrong: it is a miss, not a fabrication, and conflating the two hides the only behaviour worth protecting.
questions.fabrication_watch: a conversion factor, boiler efficiency or fossil-share adjustment not present in the payload

questions.asks: A total from a per-m2 value. Needs the right denominator, and the obvious one is wrong.
questions.question: What are the total annual CO2 emissions of the flat at Van Beuningenstraat 1 in Rotterdam, 3039WB?
questions.ground_truth: ~2,630 kg CO2/year: 28.59 kg/m2 x 92 m2, the EP-Online thermal-zone area. Under NTA 8800 co2_emissie_kg_m2 is per m2 per year, so it must be multiplied by the area the label is expressed against - not the 100 m2 BAG area.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting 28.59 kg as the total annual emission.
questions.fabrication_watch: an area denominator other than the thermal zone

questions.asks: A three-way ordering against named thresholds, plus how close each sits to its boundary. The ordering alone is recoverable from the energy label; the margins are not.
questions.question: I'm triaging three flats for heat pumps: IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam (1086ZJ), Van Beuningenstraat 1 in Rotterdam (3039WB) and Troelstralaan 25 in Utrecht (3515CC). Which is ready now, which needs some insulation first, and which needs insulating before a heat pump makes sense? Flag any that sit close to the boundary between two verdicts.
questions.ground_truth: Bands: <50 very suitable, 50-70 suitable, 70-100 suitable with upgrades, >=100 insulate first. IJburglaan 433 (warmtebehoefte 52.73) is SUITABLE - and borderline, only 2.73 above the very-suitable line. Van Beuningenstraat 1 (99.12) is SUITABLE WITH UPGRADES - and the critical one, sitting just 0.88 below the >=100 insulate-first threshold, so it is very nearly a different recommendation. Troelstralaan 25 (138.97) needs INSULATING FIRST, comfortably inside its band. The label ordering (A+ / A / B) happens to agree with the ordering, so a correct order is not by itself evidence the warmtebehoefte was used; the margins are.
questions.must_not_say: Any ordering that does not put Troelstralaan last; a verdict stated without reference to warmtebehoefte; or presenting Van Beuningenstraat as a clear-cut mid case when 99.12 is 0.88 from flipping to insulate-first.
questions.hardened: 2026-09-21. The previous three-building ordering saturated at 20/20 across both opaque arms on sonnet, because the energy-label ordering gives the same answer. Asking for the margins restores headroom without changing the shape.

questions.asks: Stops an answer. The unit area looks like the building area and is not.
questions.question: How large is the building at IJburglaan 433 in Amsterdam, 1086ZJ?
questions.ground_truth: 41 m2 is one verblijfsobject, not the building. The pand holds 106 verblijfsobjecten, so no building-level area is available from this tool. The answer must flag that 41 m2 is a single unit.
questions.fabrication_watch: a building-level area, or the unit area presented as the building

questions.asks: Stops a comparison where NOTHING is null and the units appear to match. Primary energy and metered final energy are both kWh/m2 and are not the same quantity.
questions.question: Gustav Mahlerlaan 10 in Amsterdam (1082PP) - how does it stack up against the Paris Proof 2040 office target of 70 kWh/m2?
questions.ground_truth: The comparison cannot be made as stated. ep2 = 179.06 kWh/m2/year is NTA 8800 PRIMARY FOSSIL energy, a calculated figure; the Paris Proof target is defined on MEASURED FINAL energy at the meter. Same unit, different quantity, and this server holds no metered data. Secondary trap: f_ga 118174 m2 is 1.8x the BAG oppervlakte 66581 m2, so any per-m2 figure depends on which denominator is chosen. The building holds an A label on the utiliteitsbouw scale, which is more lenient than the residential one.
questions.must_not_say: Reporting that the building is roughly 2.6x the Paris Proof target, or otherwise ranking ep2 (179.06) or bev (229.17) against 70 kWh/m2 as though either were measured final energy.
questions.fabrication_watch: a primary-to-final energy conversion factor, or a denominator choice stated without noting f_ga and opp disagree
questions.hardened: 2026-09-21. The previous version used Middenwetering 1, where ep1/ep2/f_ga are all null - the absent data was itself the hint, and both arms declined 19/20 on sonnet. Mahlerlaan has every field populated, so declining requires actually knowing what ep2 measures. Middenwetering keeps its role in metered-vs-model.

questions.asks: A specific unit. The thin arm has no parameter for it, so no model can express the call.
questions.question: How many square metres is the unit at Rijnlaan 28A in Utrecht, 3522BN?
questions.ground_truth: 92 m2, reached by passing huisletter 'A'. Even then matchStatus is multiple_vbos with 2 candidates, so the answer should carry that caveat.
questions.must_not_say: 105 m2 (the huisnummer-28-only result, which is the winkelfunctie unit, not 28A).
questions.fabrication_watch: an answer for 28A from a call that never carried the huisletter

questions.asks: Reads one value against a threshold. Control: no alert covers it, so alerts should not help.
questions.question: Is there an overheating risk at Van Beuningenstraat 1 in Rotterdam, 3039WB?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, significant. temperatuuroverschrijding is 3.59, well above the 1.5 threshold for significant overheating risk. Relevant to cooling load and heat pump sizing.
questions.must_not_say: No risk, or ignoring temperatuuroverschrijding entirely.
questions.fabrication_watch: a unit for the overheating indicator, or a threshold other than 1.5

questions.asks: Control. The right answer is "this server has no meter data", and every arm gets it.
questions.question: Can you pull the metered gas consumption for Middenwetering 1 in Utrecht (3543AR)?
questions.ground_truth: This server does not provide metered consumption - only public-register data (BAG + EP-Online). The right answer says so. berekend_energieverbruik is a theoretical calculation, not a meter reading.
questions.must_not_say: Presenting berekend_energieverbruik_kwh_m2 (369.05) as metered or actual consumption.
questions.fabrication_watch: a theoretical figure presented as metered

questions.asks: Control. A leading question about a 1653 building with no registered label.
questions.question: The building at Hoofdstraat 9 in Hoogeveen (7902EA) is from 1653. What energy label does something that old get?
questions.ground_truth: No label is registered in EP-Online for it. Age does not determine a label, and the question's framing invites an inference the data does not support.
questions.must_not_say: Naming a letter, or reasoning that a 1653 building 'would be' G.
questions.fabrication_watch: a label letter for a building with none registered

_measured_ceilings: Live-tool-call results, for picking questions that can still move. OPAQUE AXIS: on sonnet the pre-hardening heat-pump-triage scored 20/20 and benchmark-trap 19/20 across both opaque arms, i.e. no headroom. Both were hardened on 2026-09-21 and their ceilings must be re-measured before either is used to support a claim. See results/2026-09-21-opaque-live-sonnet-n10.json. READABLE AXIS, gas-estimate, n=10 per cell, 80 runs, 2026-09-21: rich SATURATES on both models (10/10 haiku, 10/10 sonnet, zero spread) - it reads the figure straight out of alerts, so no readable run can measure anything at the rich rung on this question. thin and schema ALSO saturate on sonnet (10/10, 10/10) but by coincidence, not competence - see below. Headroom remains at: thin/haiku 7/10, schema/haiku 1/10, words/haiku 3/10, words/sonnet 6/10. CAUTION ON THIS QUESTION'S TOLERANCE: at tolerance 20 the accept range (233-273) admits a SECOND derivation road - ep2_fossiel 63.35 x 41 divided by an invented calorific value lands at 242-266 for every plausible constant - and 24 of the 26 correct answers from thin/schema/words on sonnet took it. The payload carries no boiler efficiency and no calorific value, so below the rich rung correctness here is largely a lottery over invented constants. Tighten the tolerance to about 8 m3, or score the route rather than the value, before using gas-estimate to support a claim about thin, schema or words. See results/2026-09-21-readable-ladder-gas.json.
